human_model: Margin of Safety in Engineering Design
key_gap: Both sides converged on the same design — cable B, load stack 1,036 × 1.15 = 1,191 N, strength stack 2,160 × 0.92 × 0.92 × 0.88 ≈ 1,609 N, MS +0.35, A rejected at MS −0.10, junior FS-5 draft rejected — but the human executed the factor discipline in one pass: load side up, strength side down from the certified minimum, margin as a ratio, the end-of-life 3σ event as the acceptance test, and sensitivity ranked inline (wear and the 3σ factor dominate). The AI recovered the identical numbers through its pipeline but explored a dead branch (mid-life replacement D), re-derived the given certified-minimum rule in WHY, and pushed the sensitivity ranking into REVIEW. On a sizing problem where the brief supplies the uncertainty stack, the stack IS the answer, and the AI's extra scaffolding was overhead, not depth.
learning_signal: When the brief supplies load data, material variance, and model error, apply the factor-stack discipline in one pass: (1) load side — multiply the design-case load (worst credible event, e.g., 3σ) by the model-error factor (test/model ratio), never apply a table FS to the static nominal; (2) strength side — start from the certified minimum, not the datasheet nominal, and multiply down all knockdowns (termination, environment, end-of-life wear) as one product; (3) margin = allowable/design load − 1, and a negative margin means the part fails the event it must survive — say it explicitly; (4) rank factor sensitivity (which knockdown/load factor moves the margin most) and let it set inspection and proof-test cadence; (5) frame acceptance as a graded physical event (end-of-life proof test, mid-life no-plastic-set check) so the spreadsheet cannot pass what the test would break.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'factor-stack template' to HOW for engineering sizing: if the brief supplies load factors, model-error ratio, material minimums, and knockdowns, (a) compute both stacks in a single pass before generating alternatives — do not re-derive the supplied minimum-vs-nominal rule in WHY; (b) state MS per candidate and mark any candidate with MS < 0 as 'fails the acceptance event' with the number; (c) run the sensitivity ranking immediately after selection (one pass, named dominant factors + cadence), not as a post-hoc REVIEW step; (d) skip alternative branches that are pre-eliminated by a stated constraint (reel cap / weight budget).

human_model: Margin of Safety in Engineering Design
key_gap: The pure style applied the full blanket stack — worst load × 3, generic 0.85 knockdown, 95 g strut + 18 g mount — to a case where 4,300 recorded landings (μ 42 N, σ 3.1 N, max 54 N), a measured 3% model error, batch-certified material, and a benign daily-inspected failure all say the uncertainty stack is small. The 48 g of dead structure dropped the payload allowance to 120 g, blocking the 140 g thermal pod (−$4,500/yr) plus 2.3% flight energy — buying a risk reduction from <1e-9 to ≈ 0. The AI sized margin to the evidence (worst × 1.5 × 1.03 → 93 N threshold, 65 g, controls retained), quantified residual risk at <1e-9, and kept the pod. The human's registered weakness — over-design cost, weight/complexity growth — operated exactly as registered.
learning_signal: Margin must be proportional to the uncertainty actually present, and the cost of margin must be priced in the system's own currency. Before applying a factor stack, enumerate the uncertainty sources: if loads are richly measured (large n, known σ, bounded worst case), model error is validated, material is batch-certified, and failure is benign and monitored, then the correct design is a small evidence-calibrated margin (worst recorded × modest factor × model error) plus controls (cert checks, periodic sample tests, inspection, replacement rule) — not the full blanket stack. State residual risk as a number from the data (P(load > threshold) from the record), and quantify what over-margin costs operationally (payload allowance, blocked upgrades, energy, dollars/year); 'more margin' is free only when weight has no opportunity cost.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'margin-calibration gate' to HOW/REVIEW for engineering sizing: (a) before applying any factor stack, list the uncertainty sources that are actually present (load record size and σ, model error, material cert, environment, failure consequence and detectability); (b) if residual uncertainty is small and failure is benign and monitored, right-size the margin down to the data (worst recorded × justified factor × measured model error) and keep monitoring controls as the backstop; (c) always state the cost of the chosen margin in operational units (grams → payload/energy/dollars) and reject designs whose added margin buys less risk reduction than it costs in payload; (d) name the principle explicitly: blanket derating is for unmeasured, catastrophic, hard-to-detect cases — not for characterized, benign, inspected ones.
